ddl:
CREATE TABLE User (
    Account_status VARCHAR(255),
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Last_login_time DATETIME,
    Login_IP VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Phone_number VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE System (
    Access_time DATETIME,
    Approval_required BOOL,
    Callback_URL VARCHAR(255),
    Enabled BOOL,
    Secret_key VARCHAR(255),
    System_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    System_domain VARCHAR(255),
    System_name VARCHAR(255),
    Token_validity_period VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Login_record (
    Expiration_time DATETIME,
    Login_IP VARCHAR(255),
    Login_time DATETIME,
    Logout_time DATETIME,
    System_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Token VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Valid BOOL,
    PRIMARY KEY (User_ID, System_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (System_ID) REFERENCES System(System_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE System_authorization (
    Authorization_time DATETIME,
    Effective BOOL,
    Expiration_time DATETIME,
    System_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (User_ID, System_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (System_ID) REFERENCES System(System_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);
gold_question: This is a comprehensive system management platform. For user management, the system maintains basic user information including user ID, username, password, phone number, and email, while recording user status information including account status, last login time, and login IP. For system management, the platform maintains basic system information including system ID, system name, system domain, and access time, records system configuration information including callback URL, secret key, and token validity period, and manages system status including whether enabled and whether approval is required. For login records, the system maintains basic login information including user ID, system ID, login time, and login IP, records session information including token and expiration time, and manages login status including validity and logout time. For system authorization relationships, the platform maintains authorization information including user ID, system ID, and authorization time, and manages authorization status including whether effective and expiration time.

The database schema named "rschema_0424" contains four tables: User, System, Login_record, and System_authorization.
The User table represents a user of the system. It has columns for Account_status, Email, Last_login_time, Login_IP, Password, Phone_number, User_ID, and Username. These columns are all of type VARCHAR(255) and allow null values. The User_ID is the primary key of this table.
The System table represents a system that the users can access. It has columns for Access_time, Approval_required, Callback_URL, Enabled, Secret_key, System_ID, System_domain, System_name, and Token_validity_period. These columns are all of type VARCHAR(255) or BOOL and allow null values. The System_ID is the primary key of this table.
The Login_record table represents a login record of a user to a system. It has columns for Expiration_time, Login_IP, Login_time, Logout_time, System_ID, Token, User_ID, and Valid. The columns System_ID and User_ID are foreign keys referencing the System and User tables respectively. The combination of User_ID and System_ID is the primary key of this table.
The System_authorization table represents the authorization of a user to a system. It has columns for Authorization_time, Effective, Expiration_time, System_ID, and User_ID. The columns System_ID and User_ID are foreign keys referencing the System and User tables respectively. The combination of User_ID and System_ID is the primary key of this table.
This schema ensures referential integrity by enforcing foreign key constraints. When a record in the User or System table is deleted, the corresponding records in the Login_record and System_authorization tables will be automatically deleted to maintain the integrity of the data.
